summary: Legacy R script fits an unpenalised binomial/logit glm (glm.final) predicting default.payment.next.month on the UCI Taiwan credit-card data. Preprocessing: read.csv (make.names renames 'default payment next month'), lowercase column names, drop id, recode education {0,4,5,6}->4 and marriage 0->3, recode repayment-status columns pay_0..pay_6 (positions 6..11 after id removal) values {-2,-1,0}->0, convert sex/education/marriage/response to factors. caret::createDataPartition makes a stratified 70/30 split (replaced by the harness split). 15 coefficients; R converged in 6 IRLS iterations.

preprocessing.description: Read CSV with check.names=TRUE: make.names turns 'default payment next month' into 'default.payment.next.month'; other names unchanged. Rows keep raw file order (row names 1..30000).
Lower-case every column name (ID->id, LIMIT_BAL->limit_bal, PAY_0->pay_0, ...).
Drop the id column. Column positions shift: after this, column 1 = limit_bal, 2 = sex, 3 = education, 4 = marriage, 5 = age, 6 = pay_0, 7 = pay_2, 8 = pay_3, 9 = pay_4, 10 = pay_5, 11 = pay_6.

Positional loop over columns 6..11 (1-based, after id removal) = pay_0, pay_2, pay_3, pay_4, pay_5, pay_6: values -2, -1, 0 set to 0. Assigning the double 0 makes these columns numeric (meta.json confirms). pay_4 is recoded but not used in the model.

preprocessing.r_code: raw.credit$sex <- as.factor(raw.credit$sex); raw.credit$education <- as.factor(raw.credit$education); raw.credit$marriage <- as.factor(raw.credit$marriage)
preprocessing.description: Convert sex (levels 1,2), education (levels 1,2,3,4 after recode) and marriage (levels 1,2,3 after recode) to factors; reference level is the first (numerically sorted) level.
Response converted to factor with levels '0','1'; glm models P(level '1') = P(default).

preprocessing.r_code: intraining <- createDataPartition(y=raw.credit$default.payment.next.month, p=0.7, list=F); train.batch <- raw.credit[intraining,]; test.batch <- raw.credit[-intraining,]
preprocessing.description: Random stratified 70/30 split by caret. Not re-implemented: the harness supplies the R train/test membership (split.csv).

model.formula: default.payment.next.month ~ limit_bal + sex + education + marriage + pay_0 + pay_2 + pay_3 + pay_5 + pay_6 + pay_amt1 + pay_amt2

randomness: caret::createDataPartition(y=default.payment.next.month, p=0.7, list=FALSE) stratified random split; the original notebook set no seed (harness used seed 2026). Python never re-splits: train/test membership comes from output/m2_taiwan/model/reference/split.csv (R-RNG-01).
risks: GOV-01: protected attributes sex, education and marriage are direct model inputs (age is not used). Migrated faithfully; fairness must be assessed in validation (UK Equality Act 2010, FCA Consumer Duty).

Reproducibility: the original notebook used createDataPartition with no set.seed, so the legacy split (and coefficients) cannot be reproduced exactly; the parity reference relies on the harness seed 2026.

Several recode lines (education, marriage, factor conversion) are marked [reconstructed] in the source, i.e. not printed in the published notebook; the migration reproduces the script as given, but the script itself may differ from the original model.

Recoding pay_* values -2,-1,0 to 0 and then treating pay_* as linear numeric terms imposes a linear effect of months-delayed; pay_4 is recoded but excluded from the formula (and pay_amt3..6, bill_amt*, age are excluded) without documented rationale.
Education code 0 and codes 5, 6 (undocumented / 'unknown') are merged into 4 ('others'), mixing missing-information codes with a real category.
Positional column access (seq(6, 11)) is fragile: any change in the input column order would silently recode different columns.
